speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-month-old boy experiencing feeding difficulties and abdominal distension. To understand what might be wrong, have you noticed any vomiting, particularly if it appears green or bile-stained, and has your weight gain been adequate for your age?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information; the tenderness is a significant clue. Does the vomiting occur after every feeding, and has the baby passed any stool or gas recently? Please tell me if the stool looks pale, clay-colored, or if there has been no stool at all in the last 24 hours. REQUEST TEST: Abdominal_X-Ray.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Dilated bowel segments with absence of gas in the rectum, suggesting a possible obstruction

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on the X-ray showing dilated bowel segments and an absence of gas in the rectum, I suspect a mechanical obstruction. Can you confirm if there has been any passage of meconium in the first 24 hours of life, and do you recall if there were any episodes of bilious vomiting since birth? REQUEST IMAGES: Abdominal_Ultrasound.

speaker: Patient
text: There has not been fever, vomiting, or diarrhea like a stomach infection. The baby was born at 39 weeks without birth complications.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Meconium ileus (suspected cystic fibrosis). I request a sweat chloride test and a Hirschsprung disease screening (rectal biopsy) to confirm. Please ensure the baby receives IV fluids immediately to prevent dehydration.
